title: Contact & testing feedback
description: Send GUS demo feedback, installation problems and questions through the contact link.
body:
GET IN TOUCH

Found an edge?
Tell me where.

Questions, testing notes and useful bug reports are welcome. Use the contact button to open your email app; the address is not displayed on the page.

Make a bug report useful.

Include North Georgia or DIY, your platform, the build/version, what you tried, what you expected and what happened. A screenshot or an exact error message can help.

Please remove private documents, personal location details and sensitive information before sharing. If a source answer looks wrong, include the question and the relevant citation or page.

Uses your default email app. Nothing is sent automatically.

JUST WANT TO SUPPORT?

A coffee helps the next iteration.

Feedback is valuable whether or not you donate. Support is optional.

title: GUS DIY — build your own knowledge drive
description: Build a portable Windows reference library from your own documents, manuals, notes and GPS files with the GUS DIY testing demo.
body:
02 / GUS DIY

Make a drive
that knows your world.

GUS DIY is the generic edition: a small core library plus the readable reference files you choose. Build a local knowledge drive for a hobby, workshop, project or personal field library.

Bring your own useful.

Collect your manuals, notes, saved web pages, PDFs and GPS files. GUS preserves the reference files, extracts readable content, builds a local index and retrieves source passages when you search or ask.

Adding files builds an index; it does not retrain the language model or turn imperfect source material into verified advice.

Download the Windows demo ↗DIY setup guide →

DIY Android is unfinished and is not supplied. The North Georgia APK is a different edition.

YOUR KNOWLEDGE DRIVE
▱ OWNER_FILES
PDF Equipment manuals
TXT Workshop notes
HTML Saved reference pages
GPX Your route files
EXAMPLE LIBRARY / YOU CHOOSE THE CONTENT

FROM EMPTY FOLDER TO USEFUL LIBRARY

Build it around what matters to you.

  1. Give the full app a home

    Extract the complete DIY demo to a new folder on your Windows computer, USB drive or external SSD. Keep the launcher, System and OWNER_FILES together.

  2. Collect a small starter library

    Choose a few documents you have permission to use. Clear, searchable text is easier to verify than a large stack of scans. Keep your originals and backups elsewhere.

  3. Add and scan

    Copy supported files into the top-level OWNER_FILES folder. Open GUS DIY, choose My Files, then Scan My Files. Refresh alone does not import documents.

  4. Ask one concrete question

    Start with a question whose answer you can check in a known document. Inspect the numbered citation; for a PDF, use View Cited Page to check the original image.

  5. Test, refine, back up

    Check edits, rescans and restart behavior on a test library. Add files gradually. Safely eject a portable drive after the app has closed and all writes finish.

Ideas for your own drive.

01

A workshop reference shelf

Your equipment manuals, inspection notes and parts information. Check exact specifications against the original page.

02

A hobby or project library

Organize your own reference notes, saved pages and readable PDFs around the topics you return to.

03

A personal route collection

Bring your own GPX, KML or KMZ material. Imported geometry is a reference; it does not confirm current conditions or permission.

title: Install the demos on your drive or Android phone
description: Detailed setup instructions for the complete GUS Windows portable demos, building a DIY drive and installing the North Georgia Android APK.
body:
THE FIELD GUIDE TO GETTING STARTED

Set up your copy.
Keep the whole folder.

Choose the Windows portable demo for a computer or drive, or the North Georgia APK for a compatible Android phone. These are test builds with known issues.

Windows / USB drive ↓Android APK ↓DIY files ↓Updates & backups ↓

01 / WINDOWS & YOUR OWN DRIVE

A portable folder, not a single EXE.

Before you begin

Use a 64-bit Windows 10/11 PC. Allow at least 12 GB free on your PC while joining and extracting North Georgia; its extracted Windows app is about 4 GB. You can then copy the extracted folder to your portable drive. DIY is about 1.6 GB extracted; allow at least 4 GB free for its ZIP and extracted copy. A 16 GB or larger USB drive or external SSD leaves useful room for your files. Actual download sizes appear on the download page.

  1. Download the correct complete ZIP

    Open Downloads. For North Georgia Windows, save both .zip.001 and .zip.002 parts in the same folder. For DIY, save the single Windows ZIP. Wait for every download to finish. The North Georgia APK is a separate download.

  2. Check the download

    Compare the ZIP SHA-256 with the checksum published beside the release. In PowerShell, use Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "C:\path\to\download.zip". Check the release page and expected filename before running an unsigned demo.

  3. Join the North Georgia parts (DIY skips this step)

    In File Explorer, open the folder containing both parts. Type cmd in its address bar and press Enter to open Command Prompt there. Run copy /b "GUS-North-Georgia-Windows-Demo.zip.001"+"GUS-North-Georgia-Windows-Demo.zip.002" "GUS-North-Georgia-Windows-Demo.zip". This creates the complete ZIP and leaves both parts intact. Wait for it to finish, then check the joined ZIP against its separate checksum. Do not try to extract a part on its own.

  4. Extract everything

    Right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All. Choose a new local folder outside OneDrive. Do not open the app from inside the ZIP. Wait until extraction finishes.

  5. Copy the whole folder to your drive

    If you extracted to your PC first, copy the complete extracted app folder to the USB drive or external SSD. Keep the top-level EXE, System and OWNER_FILES together. Never move only the EXE.

  6. Open the top-level launcher

    Run GUS North Georgia.exe or G.U.S. DIY.exe from the extracted app folder. Read the app terms and disclaimer. Windows may identify the unsigned demo as unrecognized; only proceed if you trust the source and have verified the file. Do not disable Windows protection globally.

  7. Check a small task before travelling

    Let initialization finish. Open a bundled source, try a search and check its citation. For North Georgia, open the offline map. Close the app before disconnecting your drive, and use Windows Safely Remove Hardware.

Slow flash drives can take many minutes to copy thousands of files. A faster USB 3 drive or external SSD usually feels better. Mac and Linux builds are not provided.

02 / NORTH GEORGIA ANDROID

Install once. Carry it on your phone.

Check compatibility

Android 8.0+ on a 64-bit ARM device (arm64-v8a), at least 5 GB free internal storage, and 6 GB RAM recommended; 8 GB or more is more comfortable. The APK is about 1.6 GB. This is a debug-signed demo, not a Play Store production release. No iPhone or DIY Android app is supplied.

  1. Get the APK onto the phone

    Download the North Georgia Android v53 APK directly on your phone, or copy it from your computer or USB drive into Downloads. A USB adapter may be needed for a flash drive. Use a stable connection for this large file.

  2. Open it in Files or My Files

    Tap the completed .apk download in Android’s file manager. If Android asks, permit Install unknown apps only for the file manager or browser you are deliberately using for this download. Device wording varies.

  3. Let Android finish installing

    Confirm Install and leave the installer alone until it finishes. If installing from USB, keep the drive connected. Do not remove the drive or interrupt a large installation.

  4. Finish first-launch preparation

    Open GUS North Georgia. Keep it open while it copies the offline guide, model, references and regional map into private phone storage. Allow several minutes; slow storage may take longer. This step is local and does not need internet.

  5. Check status and location preferences

    Read the terms and disclaimer. Open More → Status and confirm the offline pack is ready. Grant location access only if you want phone-location features. Try Map and open a reference document before relying on the setup away from service.

  6. Add your own reference files

    Use More → My Files → Add Files or GPX/KML. Select supported files in Android’s picker. GUS copies and scans them in private storage. Keep the original files elsewhere, and use Export All My Files (.zip) for backups.

After installation, Android runs from internal storage; the USB drive is no longer needed. You can turn off the installer’s Install unknown apps permission again after setup. If installation fails, check completed download size, the checksum, free storage and ARM64 compatibility before retrying.

03 / BUILD YOUR DIY LIBRARY

Your documents go in OWNER_FILES.

On Windows, open My Files → Open OWNER_FILES Folder. Add supported PDF, Markdown, TXT, HTML/HTM, DOCX, GPX, KML or KMZ reference files, then choose Scan My Files. Start with copies of a few files. Scanned PDFs need extra time for local OCR on the first scan; later scans can reuse the cache.

Ask a focused question, inspect the citation and use View Cited Page for PDF evidence. OCR may misread numbers, units, symbols or tables. A successful scan does not guarantee an accurate answer. Keep maps, routes and document statements distinct from current real-world conditions.

More ways to build your own drive →

04 / KEEP YOUR WORK

Back up before every update.

  • Windows: close GUS and back up the whole old app folder and your OWNER_FILES. For a test update, extract into a separate new folder and import copies of your files. Do not overwrite personal folders with the clean demo’s empty folders.
  • Android: export My Files and retain originals before updating. Version 53 uses the existing preview signing identity. An APK with the same app ID and certificate can normally update in place; do not uninstall just to work around a signing error.
  • Uninstalling or clearing Android storage deletes private app copies. Export documents, notes, photos and saved routes first.
  • There is no automatic Windows/Android sync. Use the apps’ My Files export/import ZIP tools and transfer the ZIP yourself. A backup is not a guarantee that every app preference migrates.
Report an installation problem →

title: Demo status & known issues
description: What remains unfinished in the GUS North Georgia and DIY demos, including answer quality, map access, performance, OCR and platform limits.
body:
PLEASE READ BEFORE TESTING

A useful experiment.
Not a finished product.

GUS is offered as a demo for testing. Bugs, incomplete answers and rough edges remain. Downloading a full package does not mean full product acceptance or reliable advice.

What to watch for.

01

Answers can be incomplete

Some questions abstain even when related material exists. Broader responses can include extra passages, repetition or missing conditions. Citations establish where text came from, not that an answer is complete or correct.

02

Maps do not establish access

A route, boundary or mapped ramp does not prove a legal entrance, opening time, gate status, road condition or activity permission. Check the current situation independently.

03

Scans and tables need checking

OCR can misread values and units, and complex tables or scans can lose structure. Inspect the cited PDF page before using a measurement or critical instruction.

04

Cold starts can be slow

The measured first geographic Ask still took about 12 seconds after process restart. Local answers depend on device resources. Large imports, copying and first-launch preparation take time.

05

Platform scope matters

Windows uses static planning rather than live GPS. Android routing is limited to bundled North Georgia coverage. DIY Android, iOS, macOS and Linux downloads are not supplied.

06

Test backups and updates

The demos have unsigned Windows executables and a debug-signed Android APK. Export and retain your files. Uninstalling Android or clearing storage removes private app data.

CURRENT BUILD NOTES

What changed in North Georgia v53?

The Android map now hides unselected saved tracks, including old lines that used to reappear near Ellijay on zooming out. Opening your saved route still selects its own line. Catalogue reuse and a faster vector reader reduce repeated work without changing the bundled databases, models or ranking rules.

On the test devices, the warm Map page took about 0.3 seconds and Explore about 0.5 seconds. A cold geographic Ask dropped from about 21 to 12 seconds. The Windows card-to-map journey dropped from about 14 to 2 seconds. These are individual measurements, not guarantees for your hardware or every query.

Broader full-answer acceptance remains open. There are still answer-procedure test failures and a historical replay fixture that was unavailable for a wider check. A corrected Android source-navigation test compiled but was not rerun after device authorization ended.

Send testing feedback ↗

title: Licenses, attribution & privacy
description: Bundled third-party notices, local app data, optional links and privacy information for the GUS demo website.
body:
THE SMALL PRINT, IN PLAIN LANGUAGE

Keep the references.
Keep the notices.

GUS combines its own interface and branding with third-party software, models, maps and reference material. Those components keep their own terms and attribution.

Third-party content travels with the apps.

Keep the bundled LICENSES and runtime notice directories when copying or sharing a demo. They include notices for the local model, llama.cpp, dictionary material, map engine/data, routing data, voice and other dependencies where supplied. Third-party licenses are not replaced by this website or by the demo label.

Relevant components include Gemma (its terms and prohibited-use policy), Organic Maps and OpenStreetMap data, Wiktionary contributors through Kaikki, and packaged runtime dependencies. Sources and reference records inside the app provide further attribution. Check the license files for the specific component and build.

The project owner confirmed completion of the redistribution review on November 7, 2026. Older personal-preview wording is retained in the original package documentation as build history. These downloads are offered as testing demos, not as a finished or professionally validated product.

Your files and this website.

The website does not ask you to upload your library, run the model in your browser or create an account. This site adds no analytics, advertising scripts or cookies. The hosting provider and linked services may process ordinary connection information under their own policies.

The apps copy or index your files locally as described in their own Help and terms. Android uses private app storage; Windows uses its portable folders. Optional external links, email, GitHub downloads and Ko-fi open those services. Review a document’s sensitivity and permissions before importing or sharing it.

Contact about a license or privacy question →

title: North Georgia Adventure Drive
description: An experimental offline North Georgia reference and adventure-planning drive for Windows and Android.
body:
01 / NORTH GEORGIA ADVENTURE DRIVE

Know your corner.
Carry it with you.

A regional reference library for North Georgia, with local search, source passages, outdoor guidance, maps and your own trip documents. Available as complete Windows and Android testing demos.

WHAT YOU CAN USE IT FOR

A field library for
the planning part.

  • Look into a trip. Browse hiking, camping, paddling, fishing, cycling and motorcycle-related material and stored place records.
  • Bring your references. Keep trip notes, readable PDFs, saved pages and GPX/KML files together.
  • Look up practical information. Search the guide, dictionary, figures, tables, calculators and stored reference documents.
  • Trace an answer. Follow numbered citations to inspect the stored source and its limits.
  • Plan with the map. View regional geometry, open an individual track and save supported route plans.
Get the North Georgia demos ↗Android setup →

PICK YOUR PLATFORM

The same project. Different map behavior.

WINDOWS 10 / 11

A portable planning desk.

Run the complete extracted folder from a PC, USB drive or external SSD. Windows maps support offline reference and supported static car-route planning. There is no live GPS, traffic feed or live closure service.

Install on your drive →
ANDROID 8+ / ARM64

A reference on your phone.

The APK bundles the Organic Maps engine and North Georgia map data. With permission, it can use phone location and calculate supported offline routes inside its map coverage. It does not need the USB connected after installation.

Install the APK →
A mapped place is not a promise of access.

Check permissions, entrances, closures, weather and source dates independently. GUS is not an emergency service or a substitute for a current map, local advice or professional guidance.

Read the known issues →
